newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Insurance Council backs call to curb spending.
newsitem.headline: NZ Insurance Council backs call to curb spending.

text.p: The Insurance Council of New Zealand on Tuesday backed a call for politicians to think long and hard before agreeing to big spending policies.
The council said such policies would push the New Zealand dollar even higher than it is at present, making it even harder for the exporters who earn New Zealand's foreign exchange receipts.

Chief executive of the Insurance Council David Sargeant said the general insurance industry supported a call by Reserve Bank of New Zealand governor Don Brash for an incoming government to be circumspect in plans for big spending.
Brash told a Federated Farmers meeting in Invercargill on Monday the continued rapid rise of the currency would hurt export growth and controlling fiscal stimulus was a way of reducing that risk.

Sargeant said that when critical industries in New Zealand such as the export sector were struggling, that eventually flowed through to all other sectors, including insurance. It was important to the whole economy that the export sector remained viable, he said. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
